lessons.title: Atlas’s name and colors take root
lessons.subtitle: The club traces its identity to a Guadalajara café and an English school.

story.title: A name from mythology
story.body: Atlas says its founders chose the name of the Titan and adopted red and black after the tradition of Ampleforth College in England.

story.title: A Guadalajara beginning
story.body: The club’s anniversary account dates its foundation to 15 August 1916 at Café Rimans, placing its earliest story in the city where it began.

facts.label: Foundation date
facts.prompt: On what date does Atlas FC’s anniversary account say the club was founded at Café Rimans?
facts.evidence: The official account states that Atlas FC was founded on 15 August 1916 at Café Rimans in Guadalajara.

facts.label: Club name
facts.prompt: Which mythological figure does Atlas FC name as the source of its club name?
facts.evidence: Atlas FC says it took its name from the Titan Atlas.

facts.label: Club colors
facts.prompt: Which English school tradition does Atlas FC credit for its red-and-black colors?
facts.evidence: Atlas FC says its red-and-black colors were inspired by the tradition of Ampleforth College in England.

lessons.title: Camilo Vargas’s penalty saves end a seven-decade wait
lessons.subtitle: Atlas credits Vargas’s penalty saves with helping end a 70-year wait for another Liga MX title.

story.title: A drought broken
story.body: Atlas says Camilo Vargas stopped penalty kicks at the decisive point in its Liga MX title run, ending a 70-year championship drought.

story.title: A keeper at the turning point
story.body: The club credits those saves with guiding Atlas to the league title. The official profile records the defining action as penalty stops.

facts.label: Title drought
facts.prompt: How many years without a Liga MX title did Atlas FC say Camilo Vargas’s penalty saves helped end?
facts.scope: Atlas league-title drought before the Apertura 2021 breakthrough
facts.evidence: Atlas says Vargas stopped penalties that broke a 70-year title drought.

facts.label: Decisive goalkeeper
facts.prompt: Which Atlas FC goalkeeper does the club credit with penalty saves that helped end its 70-year Liga MX title drought?
facts.evidence: The official Camilo Vargas feature names him as the keeper whose penalty saves guided Atlas to the title.

facts.label: Title-deciding action
facts.prompt: What decisive action does Atlas FC say Camilo Vargas took during the Liga MX title run that ended the club’s 70-year drought?
distractors: Saving a penalty during regular time
facts.scope: Atlas’s league-title run ending the club’s 70-year drought; Atlas’s May 2026 profile attributes the key action to Vargas’s penalty saves.
facts.evidence: Atlas says Vargas stopped penalties that broke the 70-year title drought and guided the club to the Liga MX title.

lessons.title: Atlas turns one crown into a dynasty
lessons.subtitle: The club’s 2021–22 run paired consecutive league titles with a further national trophy.

story.title: A repeat achieved
story.body: Atlas describes Camilo Vargas as central to the extraordinary Liga MX bicampeonato, a repeat league-title achievement.

story.title: A further trophy
story.body: The club says the consecutive league crowns were sealed with a Campeón de Campeones trophy, carrying the run beyond the league itself.

facts.label: Title era
facts.prompt: Which two-season period does Atlas FC cite for the organizational transformation that led to its historic bicampeonato?
facts.evidence: Atlas identifies 2021–22 as the period of the transformation that led to its historic bicampeonato.

facts.label: Consecutive league crowns
facts.prompt: What does Atlas FC call its consecutive Liga MX title achievement in the 2021–22 period?
facts.scope: Atlas league titles in consecutive seasons
facts.evidence: Atlas calls the achievement a Liga MX bicampeonato.

facts.label: Trophy that sealed the run
facts.prompt: Which trophy does Atlas FC say sealed its consecutive-title bicampeonato after the 2021–22 transformation?
facts.evidence: The club says the bicampeonato was sealed with the Campeón de Campeones trophy.

lessons.title: From Zamora to Atlas

story.body: Barcelona signed him from Monaco in 2003, at age 24, after four seasons in France.

lessons.title: Márquez starts in the 2006 Champions League final

lessons.title: A penalty save on Atlas’s 110th anniversary

facts.evidence: The club’s match account says the penalty was awarded and saved in minute 82.

lessons.title: Vargas on the Copa América final stage
lessons.subtitle: His saves helped Colombia hold Argentina until extra time.

story.title: A final for Colombia
story.body: Camilo Vargas started in goal for Colombia against Argentina in the 2024 Copa América final. In the 57th minute, he diverted Ángel Di María’s powerful shot for a corner.

story.title: The extra-time breakthrough
story.body: The match remained scoreless through normal time. Vargas made another save in extra time, but Lautaro Martínez eventually beat him in the 112th minute to decide the final.

facts.label: Copa América final opponent
facts.prompt: Which country did Camilo Vargas face as Colombia’s starting goalkeeper in the 2024 Copa América final?
facts.scope: Camilo Vargas, Colombia, 2024 Copa América final against Argentina.
facts.evidence: CONMEBOL lists Vargas as Colombia’s starting goalkeeper against Argentina.

facts.label: Di María save
facts.prompt: In which minute did Vargas divert Ángel Di María’s powerful shot for a corner in the 2024 Copa América final?
facts.scope: Camilo Vargas, Colombia, 2024 Copa América final against Argentina.
facts.evidence: The match report locates the save at 57 minutes.

facts.label: Extra-time breakthrough
facts.prompt: Which Argentina forward beat Camilo Vargas for the winning goal in the 112th minute of the 2024 Copa América final?
facts.scope: Camilo Vargas, Colombia, 2024 Copa América final against Argentina.
facts.evidence: The report and scoring log identify Lautaro Martínez at 112 minutes.

lessons.title: Santos wins the return leg but loses the 2011/12 Concacaf final
lessons.subtitle: Santos beat Monterrey in Torreón, but Monterrey advanced on the 3–2 aggregate score.

story.title: A home-leg win
story.body: In the 2011/12 Concacaf Champions League final return leg, Santos defeated Monterrey 2–1 at Estadio Corona on 25 April 2012.

story.title: The aggregate decides it
story.body: Daniel Ludueña scored Santos’s opener, but Monterrey advanced 3–2 on aggregate and won the tournament.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Santos Laguna host CF Monterrey in the 2011/12 Concacaf Champions League final return leg?

facts.evidence: Concacaf’s official history dates the return leg to 25 April 2012 at Estadio Corona.

facts.scope: Two-leg 2011/12 Concacaf Champions League final; Santos won the second leg 2–1 but lost 3–2 aggregate.
facts.evidence: Concacaf’s official history records Santos 2–1 Monterrey in the return leg and Monterrey advancing 3–2 on aggregate.

lessons.title: Monterrey overturns Santos’s 2013 first-leg lead
lessons.subtitle: A 4–2 return-leg win turned the Concacaf final after Santos had led by two goals.

story.title: A two-goal advantage
story.body: Santos had won the first leg 2–0 in the 2013 Concacaf final. Monterrey needed a major response in the return leg.

story.title: The comeback lands
story.body: On 1 May 2013, Monterrey won the return match 4–2. Aldo de Nigris scored twice as Rayados secured a third consecutive tournament title.

facts.evidence: Concacaf dates the return-leg comeback to 1 May 2013.

facts.label: Return-leg score

facts.scope: CF Monterrey vs Santos Laguna, 2013 Concacaf final return leg
facts.evidence: Concacaf reports Monterrey won the return leg 4–2.

facts.label: Monterrey scorer
